items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: The other thing that they recorded was a thing called... [context implies Dexter Gordon was in the band] ...Dexter was about 21 then... I remember that the weather was still warm... So Billy, when we got ready to do this recording date... featured the tenors of Gene Ammons and Dexter Gordon

ctx.x: giving him a hard time, like "You're so straight" -- he got kind of whittled down to size. Which I felt sorry for him, really.

But anyway, to get ahead of the story a little... About Lucky Thompson. Later we played Boston, Massachusetts, and Lucky just went to Billy Eckstine and told him, "Look, I've had enough of this. I can't stand it any more. These guys are doing everything" and so-and-so-and-so. So Lucky quit the band. And that was when they sent and got Dexter Gordon.

After we played Cincinnati, where Gene Ammons joined us, we went to Chicago and we played, I think, the Regal Theatre. Then I think after that we played either Pittsburgh or Detroit -- I don't remember. But then we went to Boston and we played Boston in this old club up there that all the big bands used to broadcast. We might have been one of the last big bands to go in there. I can't remember the name of the club right now, but it was quite a famous club back in the Thirties [THE SOUTHLAND?]. Because I used to…
